subproblem.title: Blow-ups of a region boundary are region boundaries: η_{y,λ#}∂[[E]] = ∂[[η_{y,λ}(E)]] with orientation ξ_N(y + λ·)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, E ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. Let η := η_{y,λ} (dilation y λ, η(z) = λ^{−1}(z − y)) and η_#T := blowUp T y λ ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)). If T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N, H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1]), then η_#T(ω) = ∫_{η(E)} ξ_N(y + λw)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(η(U)), i.e. IsBoundaryOfRegion (blowUp T y λ) (η(E)) (w ↦ ξ_N(y + λw)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → IsBoundaryOfRegion (blowUp T y lam hlam.ne') (dilation y lam '' E) (fun w => ξN (y + lam • w))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 1 (first three bullets) of the supplied proof of the parent node: the representation of S_i = η_{x_i,λ_i#}T as a region boundary. Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω), chapter-06.txt line 408) and Simon 7.5.1 (T = ∂[[E]], chapter-07.txt line 752). Sibling children used: testform_corr (Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr) and blowup_change_of_variables (Submission.setIntegral_blowUpMap_image_eq_inv_pow_mul). Neither measurability of E nor openness of U is needed.

Notation. η := dilation y λ, η(z) = −λ^{−1}y + λ^{−1}z = λ^{−1}(z − y). H^{n+1} := μHE[n+1]. dβ := exteriorDerivative β. For a j-covector β and c ∈ ℝ, β(cv_1, …, cv_j) = c^j·β(v_1, …, v_j) (multilinearity; ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ).

1. (Test-form correspondence.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^n(η(U)) (TestFormOn (dilation y λ '' U) n). By testform_corr (a) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with ω'(z) = ω(η(z)) for all z ∈ ℝ^P, and by testform_corr (c), blowUp T y λ (ω) = λ^{−n}·T(ω').

2. (Hypothesis.) IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N applied to ω' gives T(ω') = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω'(z)) dH^{n+1}(z).

3. (Exterior derivative of ω' = ω∘η.) Let L := λ^{−1}·id (dilationCLM P λ) and b := −λ^{−1}y, so η(z) = b + Lz, and let φ := affinePullbackForm L b ω, i.e. φ(z)(v_1, …, v_n) = ω(η(z))(λ^{−1}v_1, …, λ^{−1}v_n) = λ^{−n}·ω(η(z))(v_1, …, v_n). Thus ω' = λ^n·φ as forms. ω is a test form, in particular smooth, so SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm gives dφ = affinePullbackForm L b (dω), i.e. dφ(z)(v_0, …, v_n) = dω(η(z))(λ^{−1}v_0, …, λ^{−1}v_n) = λ^{−(n+1)}·dω(η(z))(v_0, …, v_n). By linearity of d (exteriorDerivative_smul), dω'(z) = λ^n·dφ(z) = λ^{−1}·dω(η(z)) for every z.

4. (Pulling out the scalar.) Each ξ_N(z) is linear, so steps 2–3 give T(ω') = ∫_E λ^{−1}·ξ_N(z)(dω(η(z))) dH^{n+1}(z) = λ^{−1}·∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(η(z))) dH^{n+1}(z) (integral_const_mul; no integrability is needed).

5. (Rewriting the integrand.) Put g(w) := ξ_N(y + λw)(dω(w)) for w ∈ ℝ^P. For every z, y + λ·η(z) = y + (z − y) = z, hence ξ_N(z)(dω(η(z))) = g(η(z)).

6. (Change of variables.) SimonGMT blowUpMap y λ is z ↦ λ^{−1}(z − y) = −λ^{−1}y + λ^{−1}z, i.e. blowUpMap y λ = η as functions. By blowup_change_of_variables (with n + 1 in place of n, M := E, x := y, r := λ, f := g): ∫_{η(E)} g dH^{n+1} = λ^{−(n+1)}·∫_E g(η(z)) dH^{n+1}(z). Hence ∫_E g(η(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) = λ^{n+1}·∫_{η(E)} g dH^{n+1}.

7. (Conclusion.) By steps 1, 4, 5 and 6: blowUp T y λ (ω) = λ^{−n}·λ^{−1}·λ^{n+1}·∫_{η(E)} g dH^{n+1} = ∫_{η(E)} ξ_N(y + λw)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w). Since ω ∈ 𝒟^n(η(U)) was arbitrary, IsBoundaryOfRegion (blowUp T y λ) (η(E)) (w ↦ ξ_N(y + λw)). ∎
proof_key_steps: blowUp T y λ (ω) = λ^{−n}·T(ω∘η) with ω∘η ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (testform_corr).
ω∘η = λ^n·(affine pull-back of ω) and d commutes with affine pull-back, so d(ω∘η) = λ^{−1}·(dω)∘η.
ξ_N(z) = ξ_N(y + λη(z)); the change of variables ∫_E g∘η dH^{n+1} = λ^{n+1}∫_{η(E)} g dH^{n+1} (blowup_change_of_variables) cancels all powers of λ.

audit.reason: The proof establishes the exact contract for arbitrary U and E. Test-form correspondence, exterior differentiation and the accepted change-of-variables identity cancel the scaling factors correctly without imposing measurability or integrability hypotheses.
